name: bantou
description: bantou-server commands (kick_cap, stop_cap, status, hello, update_server, task, worker_reply, retire_server), replies (cap_result, stop_result, status_result, hello_result, update_result, task_result, worker_reply_result, retire_result, error) and notices (activity, worker_report). Message body is one JSON object in the text; `bantou: 1` is the body schema version.

hello.description: Ask the server for its own version and update state. Reply: hello_result. Accepted whatever the sender's protocol version is. The shape of hello / hello_result / update_server / update_result is fixed (they are how a server of another protocol version is updated).

server_version.description: npm `bantou` version of the running server.

protocol_version.description: Registered messenger protocol version of the running server.

server_id.description: Stable id of this server (generated once per workspace, kept in <workspace>/server.json). Since 1.7.0; absent from an older server - fall back to the messenger peer id.

host.description: os.hostname() of the server's machine. Since 1.7.0.

user.description: OS user the server runs as. Since 1.7.0.

workspace.description: Absolute workspace path of the server. Since 1.7.0.

update.description: The update in progress, or null.

last_update.description: The last failed update (kept until the next attempt), or null.

reports.description: Worker reports still being handled (a cap resume pending).

update_server.description: Tell the server to update itself to npm `bantou@<version>` and restart after every running cap / worker is done. While it waits, kick_cap and task are refused with error code `updating` (retryable). Reply: update_result or error. The package source is the server's config, never this message.

kick_cap.description: Start or resume the remote cap `cap_id` headlessly with `prompt`. Reply: cap_result or error.

repo.description: Git URL; cloned into the cap path on first use, fetched afterwards. Must not start with '-'.

branch.description: Branch for git clone --branch. Must not start with '-'.

model.description: Model of the cap's own claude -p, passed as-is to --model. Absent = no --model. Servers older than 1.4.0 ignore it.

worker_model.description: Default model of the workers this cap starts (used when worker_start has no model). The server remembers it as the cap's default.

stop_cap.description: Stop the running remote cap `cap_id` (kills its claude process group). Reply: stop_result or error. The interrupted kick_cap still gets its own cap_result with ok=false.

stopped.description: true when a running (or about to start) run was stopped; false when the cap was not running.

status.description: List caps and workers with their state. Reply: status_result. With cap_id the server also takes the sender as the center to notify for that cap (by the sender's peer name, resolved to its current peer id at send time). Since 1.6.0 (cap_id).

cap_result.description: Outcome of one headless cap run (also sent when a worker report resumes the cap).

session_id.description: Claude session id used (new or resumed).

result_text.description: Final result text; empty when the run failed before producing one.

error.description: Failure detail when ok is false.

server_id.description: Stable id of this server (generated once per workspace, kept in <workspace>/server.json). Since 1.7.0; absent from an older server - fall back to the messenger peer id.

host.description: os.hostname() of the server's machine. Since 1.7.0.

user.description: OS user the server runs as. Since 1.7.0.

workspace.description: Absolute workspace path of the server. Since 1.7.0.

server_version.description: npm `bantou` version of the running server. Since 1.7.0.

protocol_version.description: Registered messenger protocol version of the running server. Since 1.7.0.

queued.description: Commands waiting in this agent's queue (the running one excluded).

model.description: Model the agent was started with (--model); null / absent = none given. Servers older than 1.4.0 omit it.

task.description: Give the remote cap `cap_id` a task. The server builds the cap's first instruction from goal / deliverables / verify / constraints / workers. The same cap_id again resumes the cap. Reply: task_result or error. Since 1.5.0.

repo.description: Git URL the work is based on. Must not start with '-'.

branch.description: Base branch of the work. Must not start with '-'.
Branch the workers push to. Must not start with '-'.

report_path.description: Where the workers put their reports.

steps.description: Check procedure, one step per entry.

constraints.description: Constraints, one per entry (may be empty).

workers.description: Worker split. No items = the default: at least 2 workers, one implement and one review.

id.description: Name other items refer to in depends_on.

depends_on.description: id of the items that must finish before this one starts.

worker_model.description: Default model of the workers (same as kick_cap worker_model).

task_result.description: Reply to task, taken from the cap's final answer. When no JSON could be read: summary = the raw answer, workers / remaining empty, review.verdict unknown. Since 1.5.0.

state.description: done = the run ended normally; failed = it did not (see error).

result.description: Head of the worker's result (at most 500 chars).

error.description: Failure detail when state is failed.

worker_reply.description: Send text to the worker worker_id of the cap cap_id (the server runs worker_start with the same worker_id). Reply: worker_reply_result or error. Since 1.5.0.

retire_server.description: Retire the server: refuse new work, stop every cap / worker, unregister from the messenger, release the host lock and exit (supervisor and launcher with it, exit code 76 so a service manager does not restart it). Reply: retire_result (sent before the server goes away) or error. Irreversible: the server writes <workspace>/server.retired and refuses to start until that file is removed. Accepted whatever the sender's protocol version is (control command). Since 1.8.0; a server older than that ignores it WITHOUT a reply, so a center sends it only to a server whose declared protocol version is 1.8.0 or later and never reads no-reply as retired.

server_id.description: Expected server_id of the target. A different server_id gets an error and nothing is stopped.

reason.description: Free text, logged and written to server.retired.

exit_at.description: ISO 8601. When the server starts to exit.

exit_code.description: Exit code the server leaves with (76).

host_steps.description: Shell lines for an operator with root: remove the unit, the OS user, the workspace. Values are shell-quoted.

detected.description: true = read from the running process; false = the install-service.sh default name, not confirmed.

worker_report.description: Notice from server to center (not a reply): a worker called its report tool. Sent for every report, in parallel with the resume of the cap. Since 1.5.0.

task_id.description: task_id of the latest task of the cap; absent when the cap has had no task.

activity.description: Notice from server to center (not a reply). Liveness summary of a cap and its workers, derived from their stream-json output. Sent every 5s while any agent runs, and on each state change.

agents.description: The cap first, then its workers by id.

cap_id.description: The cap itself for a cap, the owning cap for a worker.

task.description: Head of the last kick_cap / worker_start prompt (one line, at most 200 chars).

last_activity.description: Short summary of the latest activity (at most 120 chars).

last_output_at.description: When the last stdout line arrived (server clock, ISO 8601).

silent_ms.description: Milliseconds since the last output (or started_at) at send time.

error.description: Why the agent is failed / lost (at most 200 chars).

model.description: Model the agent runs with (--model); null / absent = none given. Servers older than 1.4.0 omit it.

command.description: type of the failed command, when known.

code.description: Machine-readable cause. updating = the server waits to restart for an update, resend later.

retryable.description: true when the same command may be sent again later.

retiring.description: The server is retiring (retire_server accepted) and refuses this command for good. Since 1.8.0.
